voiceover:
[conversational] The most boring tool on Instagram quietly makes about $32K every month.

And the move that got it started isn't what you'd guess. Stay till the end.

It's called Liinks. One link-in-bio page that holds your links, socials, forms and QR codes. Starter is $5 a month, Pro is $12.

[serious] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR. About $32K in monthly recurring revenue. About $31K in the last 30 days. 5,534 active subscriptions, growing 3% a month. One person runs it: Charlie Clark, bootstrapped.

How'd it grow? Version one was free. Then he added features and charged $3 a month. Later he leaned on Google Search ads, because people searching for link-in-bio tools already want one.

[amused] Honest catch: revenue isn't profit, and close to 100 tools compete here.

[whispers] So what was the first move? Charlie was already talking to artists for his earlier marketplace. They became his first customers, and he set up their pages himself.

[confident] He didn't go find an audience. He built for one he already had.

Would you build a boring business like this, or just use one?

Send this to the friend who thinks boring businesses don't make money.

pick.angle: A 'link in bio' page, the most boring tool on Instagram, quietly makes about $32K every month

research.what_it_does: A link-in-bio and mini-website builder. One page, built from blocks, holds a creator's links, socials, forms, QR codes and an Instagram post sync.
research.who_pays: Creators and small businesses pay for a Starter plan. Pro is for professionals and teams who manage several profiles.
research.pricing: Starter is $5/month or $48/year. Pro is $12/month or $120/year, and adds multi-profile management, custom domains and API access. Both plans include a 14-day free trial (liinks.co pricing and help center). The liinks.co page says a free trial, with no free tier mentioned.
growth: Idea: Charlie Clark was running a print-on-demand art marketplace and noticed many of the artists he talked to used Linktree-style tools to share their work (Starter Story; AppSumo 'Mind Your Business' newsletter).
First users: artists from his earlier marketplace were his first customers. He did 'white-glove' onboarding and set up their pages for them (AppSumo newsletter).

Launch model: v1 was free because it was too simple to charge for. He later bundled enough features and added a $3/month Premium plan (Starter Story). AppSumo says he flipped to paid 2–3 months after launch.
Cold outreach: during the free era he targeted Instagram users who had no link-in-bio page (MoneyMint, summarizing the Starter Story interview).
Product Hunt: Clark said he launched on Product Hunt in 2021, after a soft launch at the end of January (Indie Hustle, quoting his post).

Early milestones per Indie Hustle: about 4 months later it hit $1,000 MRR, after more features, a 14-day free trial and a decent amount of paid Instagram marketing. About 2 months after that he raised the price from $3 to $3.99 and hit $2,000 MRR. It reached $15K in Dec 2022 and $20K in July 2023.

Main channel at scale: from $1–5K MRR onward he leaned on Google Search ads for link-in-bio-style terms, which AppSumo calls high intent and high ROI. Starter Story's 2025 interview summary (BigGo) calls it the easiest channel because people are actively searching.
Pricing lever: a Starter Story interview summary (BigGo) credits undercutting Linktree on price, plus a price increase of about $1 that added nearly $5,000 in MRR.
founder_story: Charlie Clark is the solo founder. His background is in design and software engineering (Starter Story).
In 2019 he quit his full-time job to build a print-on-demand marketplace for artists. Liinks came out of the outreach he did for it (Starter Story).
Liinks started in 2020 as a side project (official About page). AppSumo says about 4 years of nights and weekends got it to $27K MRR, while he kept a day job and raised a toddler.

He was a software engineer at Squarespace and built Liinks alongside that job. He reportedly waited until Liinks matched his salary, then quit in August 2024 to go full time (BigGo summary of the Starter Story video).
The About page says Liinks is independently built and operated, with no investors.
lessons: Build for a market you already talk to. The idea came from artists he was already doing outreach to, and they became his first customers.
Launch simple and free to get users, then add features and start charging. He charged only once there were enough features to justify it.
Pick one high-intent channel. Google Search ads on 'link-in-bio' terms worked in a category with close to 100 competing tools (AppSumo).
Undercut the incumbent on price, then raise prices as the product improves. The $3 to $3.99 rise and a later roughly $1 increase are both sourced.
Keep the day job until the side project can replace the salary. He quit in August 2024, after about 4 years of side-project work.
criticism: The market is crowded. AppSumo says there are close to 100 link-in-bio tools, and Linktree is the dominant incumbent.
Liinks does not sell anything. There is no product block, checkout or payments, so it competes on page design and a flat price (startupbase review).
Revenue is not profit. The data shows no costs, and Google Search ads are a major acquisition channel.
It is a one-person business, so there is key-person risk. The slow side-project path took about 4 years to reach $27K MRR.
facts: Starter Story lists Brooklyn, NY and a February 2020 start. TrustMRR says May 2020 and the About page says only 2020, so use 2020 only.
MoneyMint quotes Charlie describing Liinks as 'ramen profitable' at an earlier stage.
Features include multi-tab navigation, QR codes, forms, short links, Mailchimp and Instagram integrations, and scheduling (official Features page).
Pro plan pricing for team members: it includes 5 profiles, with extra packs of 5 for $10/month, up to 100 profiles (help center).
Charlie Clark's site, charliie.co, says he bootstrapped Liinks solo to $30k+ MRR.
do_not_claim: Profit or margin: the only source is the 'ramen profitable' quote from an earlier period.
Exact number of users. TrustMRR says ~10,000 and a liinks.us page says 10,000+, but neither is a primary stat.
That Product Hunt or the Instagram ads drove a specific number of customers.
Any exact CAC or ad spend.
That Liinks has a free plan. liinks.co shows a 14-day trial only, while a liinks.us page lists a $0 Free plan, so this is unclear.
research.notes: Use TrustMRR figures for revenue, not the older press figures. These were $20K, $25K and $27K MRR, and the two stork.ai articles quote $31,500. The three Starter Story, AppSumo and BigGo items are third-party summaries of the Starter Story interview. The 2025 interview details (the Aug 2024 quit, the roughly $1 price rise worth nearly $5K MRR) come only from BigGo's summary, so attribute them to the Starter Story interview, not to the official site. The exact on-page text for 'Pro $12/month' was not confirmed, so the pricing pages to show are the homepage pricing section (Starter $5/month) and Features. A separate domain, liinks.us, shows a Free plan. Check which domain is current before recording, and treat all on-screen text as something to verify live.
